title: feat(integrations): add Bindery (ebook/audiobook manager) as a media organizer integration
body:
## What

Adds [Bindery](https://github.com/vavallee/bindery) — a self-hosted ebook/audiobook
library manager — as a new `mediaOrganizer` integration, alongside Sonarr and Radarr.
Bindery exposes the same shape of data those already provide (missing/wanted items,
active download queue), so this implements the existing `IMediaOrganizerIntegration`
interface rather than inventing a new one.

Bindery is a book-focused counterpart to Sonarr/Radarr — this is the first integration
in this category for books specifically (Readarr/Lidarr currently only implement
`ICalendarIntegration`, not this interface).

## What's included

- `BinderyIntegration` (`packages/integrations/src/media-organizer/bindery/`):
  `getMissingAsync` against `/api/v1/wanted/missing`, `getMediaQueueAsync` against
  `/api/v1/queue` (filtered to non-`imported` rows — that endpoint returns full
  history, not just active items), `testingAsync` against the authenticated
  `/api/v1/system/status`.
- Widened `MissingMediaItem`/`QueuedMediaItem`'s `type` union to add `"book"`
  (previously `"movie" | "episode"`), with corresponding rendering support (poster
  icon/color, badge, subtitle line showing the author) in the shared `mediaMissing`
  widget component.
- A `"book"` example added to the `mediaOrganizer` mock/demo data, so the new type is
  exercised by Homarr's own demo mode, not only by a real Bindery backend.
- New `integrationDefs` entry, doc-slug entry, a docs page under
  `docs/integrations/bindery`, an `en.json` translation string, and unit tests
  (`packages/integrations/test/bindery-integration.spec.ts`) covering the
  missing/queue mapping, the imported-row filter, client-side pagination, and a
  regression case for an explicit `null releaseDate` (see Testing below).

## Icon

`iconUrl` points at the dashboard-icons CDN
(`cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons@master/svg/bindery.svg`), same as
every other integration. The corresponding [community icon
submission](https://dashboardicons.com/community/bindery) has already merged, so this
resolves correctly.

## Testing

- Full test suite, no exclusions, run three times across this PR's development: 1832
  passed, 0 real failures, 12 skipped. A handful of Docker/Testcontainers-based tests
  unrelated to this change (different ones each run — nextcloud, home-assistant,
  db/proxy-reader) failed intermittently under full-suite concurrency and passed
  cleanly every time when re-run in isolation — confirmed as pre-existing test-runner
  flakiness, not a regression from this change.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean across all 37 packages in the monorepo.
- `pnpm build` succeeds across all build targets (main app + docs site).
- Lint (`eslint` + `sherif`) clean.
- `pnpm -F @homarr/docs build` (production Docusaurus build) succeeds, generated pages
  verified to contain real content.
- Manually verified end-to-end against a live Bindery instance, not just automated
  tests: created a real integration through the UI, confirmed "Test connection and
  create" succeeds against real credentials, and confirmed the `mediaMissing` widget
  renders real missing-book and queue data with correct book-specific styling.
  Deliberately tested failure paths too — a wrong API key and an unreachable
  host/port each surface a distinct, correct error message and correctly block
  integration creation (no silent failure at that layer).

During manual testing I found and fixed one real bug: 3 of the missing books in my
test library have an explicit `"releaseDate": null` (not omitted) for titles with no
known release date yet, which the original schema (`.optional()` only) rejected.
Widened to `.optional().nullable()`, with a regression test using the exact live
payload shape.

## Found during testing, not fixed here (pre-existing, not Bindery-specific)

Two issues in shared `media-missing` code surfaced while testing this integration.
Neither is caused by or specific to Bindery — both would affect Sonarr/Radarr
identically — so I'm surfacing them here rather than bundling an unrelated fix into
this PR:

1. **Toggling `showMissing`/`showQueued` live (without a page reload) can blank the
   panel even though data is present.** `component.tsx`'s Mantine `Tabs` uses
   uncontrolled `defaultValue`; if the currently-active tab stops being rendered, the
   component doesn't fall back to the remaining tab, and the panel renders empty with
   no error. 100% reproducible. A real fix means converting to controlled tab state
   (`value`/`onChange` with a reset when the visible tab set changes).
2. **The widget can't distinguish "no data configured yet" from "the backend just
   errored."** The query hook only destructures `data`, never checks `error`/
   `isError`, so a genuine backend failure renders identically to a fresh, unconfigured
   widget. Compounding this, `packages/api/src/router/widgets/media-organizer.ts` uses
   `Promise.all()` across every integration attached to a widget, so one failing
   integration blanks the *entire* widget's data, not just its own tab.

Happy to file these as separate issues if that's useful.

title: feat: Notification widget - Support Markdown/HTML, Delete Option, and Disable Clickthrough
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I would like to request the following enhancements for the Gotify widget:

- Markdown/HTML Rendering: Render notification content properly so formatting (e.g., Markdown or HTML) is displayed correctly within the widget.
- Delete/Dismiss Functionality: Add an option to delete or hide notifications directly from the widget UI.
- Toggleable Clickthrough: Add a configuration setting to enable/disable the default clickthrough redirect to the Gotify web app. Alternatively, move the link to a dedicated small button or icon.

### Additional information

Currently, the Gotify widget has a few limitations that reduce its usability compared to using a raw iframe:

1. Formatting Issues: Notification content containing HTML or Markdown does not render correctly.
2. Management: There is no option to delete or dismiss notifications directly from the widget.
3. Navigation Behavior: Clicking a notification automatically redirects to the Gotify web interface. There is no setting to disable this clickthrough behavior, which can cause unintended navigation when interacting with the widget (especially if action buttons like delete are added).

Currently using an iframe to view and manage Gotify notifications, but a fully functional native widget would provide a much cleaner integration and better user experience.

title: feat(plex): surface newly added episodes in media releases widget
body:
Closes #6847

## Problem

`PlexIntegration.getMediaReleasesAsync()` only reads `/library/recentlyAdded`, which returns **seasons** with the season's own `addedAt`. Episodes added to a season that already exists never change that value, so the media releases widget never shows them (the widget looks stale for anyone following ongoing shows).

## Change

- Additionally fetch the most recently added episodes of every `show` library (`/library/sections/{id}/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc`, one request per show library, 50 items each).
- Seasons already in `/library/recentlyAdded` that received newer episodes are bumped to the episode's `addedAt` and use its `originallyAvailableAt` as release date.
- Seasons that fell out of `/library/recentlyAdded` but got new episodes are rebuilt from the episode metadata (`grandparentTitle` / `parentTitle`, `grandparentThumb` + `art` as images, link to the season).
- Result is sorted by `addedAt` desc and capped at 50 (Plex's default page size), so the widget behaves like Plex's own "Recently added" and like the Jellyfin integration (`Items/Latest` groups episodes into their series).
- Any failure while fetching episodes is logged and falls back to the previous behaviour, so servers/tokens without library access are unaffected.
- Small refactor: `fetchJsonAsync()` helper shared by the JSON endpoints, `recentlyAddedItemSchema` extracted so it can be reused.

## Tests

- Existing spec unchanged and passing (episode fetch fails in its mock → fallback path).
- New spec: bumped season ordering + release date, season rebuilt from episode metadata (title, images, href), and fallback when the episode endpoints error.

`pnpm --filter @homarr/integrations typecheck`, `lint` and `vitest run packages/integrations/src/plex` pass.

This PR contains the following updates:

|---|---|---|---|
| [fastify](https://fastify.dev/) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/fastify/fastify)) | [`5.9.0` → `5.12.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/fastify/5.9.0/5.12.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/fastify/5.12.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/fastify/5.9.0/5.12.1?slim=true) |

---

### fastify vulnerable to X-Forwarded-* spoofing under trustProxy hop-count
[CVE-2026-16732](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-16732) / [GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2026-3635](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-3635) ([GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf](https://redirect.github.com/fastify/fastify/security/advisories/GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf)) added a `proxyFn(socket.remoteAddress, 0)` guard on the `X-Forwarded-*` reads in `request.host`, `request.protocol`, `request.hostname`, `request.ip`, and `request.ips`. That guard closes the IP, CIDR, and custom-function forms of `trustProxy` correctly because those forms compile to predicates that inspect the connecting address. The hop-count form (`trustProxy: <number>`) compiles to a predicate that structurally ignores the address argument, so the guard reduces to `0 < tp`, always true for any `tp >= 1`.

Applications configured with `trustProxy: <number>` (documented as "behind N reverse proxies", `trustProxy: 1` being the canonical single-proxy setting) remain vulnerable. An attacker who can reach the Fastify origin directly, bypassing the front-facing proxy, can spoof the request fields exactly as in the unpatched version. Impact class matches the parent CVE-2026-3635: host injection in generated URLs, HTTPS-enforcement bypass, secure-cookie / CSRF-origin bypass, host-based routing and cache poisoning.

##### Patches

Patched in fastify 5.12.1. The numeric form of `trustProxy` is now disabled at runtime and removed from the TypeScript type union.

##### Workarounds

- Migrate to an IP / CIDR / custom-function `trustProxy` value that validates the connecting address. Custom functions must inspect the `address` argument, not only the hop index.

### Auth.js: OAuth state, nonce, and PKCE check cookies are not bound to the provider that created them
[CVE-2026-73419](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73419) / [GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Auth.js stores the OAuth/OIDC anti-CSRF checks (`state`, `nonce`, and the PKCE verifier) in global cookies that are not bound to the provider that created them. On callback, a check value minted during a sign-in started with one provider can satisfy the callback for a different provider, because the stored cookie is not verified against the callback provider's identity (provider id, issuer, client id, or redirect URI). In a multi-provider app that allows account linking while logged in, this provider-confusion / mix-up condition can let an attacker link their account at a second provider to a victim's user.

##### Am I affected?

You may be affected if **all** of the following hold:

- You use `next-auth` `<= 4.24.14` or `>= 5.0.0-beta.1, <= 5.0.0-beta.31`, or `@auth/core` `<= 0.41.2`.
- You configure multiple OAuth/OIDC providers.
- You allow users to link additional providers while logged in.
- At least one configured provider's authorization request is observable by an attacker, and at least one target provider's callback can be satisfied without a PKCE verifier (i.e. it relies only on `state` or only on `nonce`).

You are **not** affected if you use a single OAuth provider, do not allow logged-in account linking, or all providers enforce PKCE.

##### Impact

- Account-linking confusion: an attacker can get their account at a target provider linked to the victim's Auth.js user, granting the attacker persistent sign-in to the victim's account through that linked provider.
- Exploitation requires luring the victim into starting a legitimate same-origin flow; it cannot be performed by cross-site request forgery alone, which reduces practical likelihood.

##### Patched version

The fix binds the OAuth check cookies to the provider/authorization flow that created them, so a callback cannot consume a check value minted for a different provider. Upgrade to the first releases containing this fix (pending; this advisory will be updated with exact patched versions before publication).

##### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately:

- Enable PKCE (`checks: ["pkce"]`, in addition to `state`/`nonce`) on every provider that supports it; PKCE blocks the practical code-swap variant because the attacker cannot observe the relying party's verifier.
- Avoid offering logged-in account linking across multiple providers where one provider is lower-trust or attacker-observable.
- Treat `events.linkAccount` as sensitive: add audit logging, user notification, or out-of-band confirmation so that any unexpected link is visible (defense-in-depth, not a root-cause fix).

##### Credit

Reported by @​Nadav0077. Thank you for the responsible disclosure.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.8 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

title: fix(docker): report container CPU as a total-system percentage
body:
This branch started as the Unraid CPU fix for #6082. That landed separately in #6510 on 2026-08-22, so the Unraid hunk is gone and what is left is a different fix on a different file. Retitling rather than opening a new PR, so the review history stays attached.

## Problem

`calculateCpuUsage` in `packages/request-handler/src/docker.ts` divides the container's cumulative `total_usage` by the cumulative `system_cpu_usage`. Both counters run from container start, so the result is the container's lifetime average, not what it is doing now. A container that was busy an hour ago keeps reporting a high number long after the load ended.

It then multiplies by `online_cpus`, following docker stats' per-core convention, where 134% means 1.34 busy cores. Every other CPU reading in Homarr is a 0-100% share of the machine, so the same dashboard shows two different scales.

## Fix

Compare the latest reading against the previous one, which is what `precpu_stats` is for, and report the plain ratio. `system_cpu_usage` already accumulates across all cores, so the ratio is the whole-machine share and cannot exceed 100%.

`precpu_stats` is absent when stats are fetched in one-shot mode, Podman being the case that matters here, so the deltas fall back to the cumulative totals and behave as before rather than dividing by zero.

## The part worth a second opinion

Dropping the `online_cpus` multiplier changes what the number means: a container using 1.34 cores on an 8 core host reported 134% before and reports about 17% now. I think matching the rest of Homarr's 0-100% scale is the right call, but it is a visible change and it is yours to make. Say so if you would rather keep docker stats' convention and I will restore the multiplier while keeping the delta fix.

## Tests

`docker.spec.ts` covers the delta calculation, the fallback when `precpu_stats` is missing, and that several fully busy cores stay at or below 100%. The two existing expectations that encoded the old per-core scale were updated with the arithmetic spelled out.

### Describe the bug

So I noticed that when I open Homarr on my mobile device. 2 out of my 25 app are in their 'Media' category I created, but the other 3 categories I created become empty and all apps show up above the categories. I don't see anything in the logs that would indicate a problem, but I'm guessing this is all happening client side. 

I don't have any custom CSS. Everything was added through the web interface. I do have 3 layouts: small, medium, and large. And I do think that is the source of the problem. On the 'large' layout, it works as expected. If I resize to the medium layout, everything, except for those 2 apps, drop out of their respective category. 

Then I resized it so it gets the small layout, and manually added an app into a category, and that app stays in the category for small and large, and drops out again for medium. 

So does that mean I have to categorize my apps separately for each layout? That doesn't make sense to me. Shouldn't the category an app belongs to stay the same no matter what the layout is?

I put all the details on how to reproduce in the bug description.

This makes Homarr a lot less usable on mobile. At the very least, it is a huge pain to have to recategorize all my apps for each layout.
